newsitem.title: USA: Borden Foods plans to sell Cracker Jack, others.
newsitem.headline: Borden Foods plans to sell Cracker Jack, others.

text.p: Borden Foods Corp. said it plans to sell its famed Cracker Jack candy-coated popcorn and other products to focus on its core pasta and food businesses.
Borden Foods is one of 10 independent companies created under the Borden Inc. umbrella after the Columbus, Ohio-based company was taken private by investors Kohlberg Kravis Roberts in 1995.
Other units, unaffected by the Borden Foods unit's strategic plan, include gluemaker Elmer's Products, snack food maker Wise Foods and Borden/Meadow Gold Dairies, home of Elsie, the Borden Cow.

When Borden was a publicly traded company, it had sought to sell its dairies, but new management refocused that business on its strongest geographic regions west of the Mississippi River, spokesman Nick Iammartino said Thursday.
The Borden Foods unit in a statement on Wednesday that it was starting to implement a strategy sharpening its focus on pasta and other food products.
Creamettes, Prince, Catelli, Merlino's and R-F pasta brands, Classico premium pastas and sauces and Wyler's soups will be retained, Iammartino said.
"Using innovation to create value-added products ... is a key part of our strategy going forward," he said, adding the unit will also seek acquisitions in its core product areas.

Other non-core lines to be sold include Eagle Brand condensed Milk, Creamora non-dairy coffee creamer, Kava acid-reduced instant coffee, Borden's cheese business and ReaLemon reconstituted juice, Iammartino said.
